bad.title: Nothing changes next to the button
bad.text: Press Place order and this part of the form looks the same, so people press again.

bad.title: Email is scrolled out of sight
bad.text: The form opens at Street, so the Email error appears where nobody is looking.

good.title: Pressing it scrolls the form up
good.text: The view jumps to the problem instead of staying by the button.

good.title: 1 problem, said at the top
good.text: It gets focus, so screen readers announce it too.
good.wait: Press Place order to see this.

good.title: Email is missing is a link
good.text: One press puts the cursor in Email, ready to type.
good.wait: Press Place order to see this.

bad.title: Three lines for one missing domain
bad.text: “Add the part after @”, “Must include a domain” and “Must be a valid email” all mean the same.
bad.wait: Press Create account to see this.

bad.title: Four rules at once for abc
bad.text: Length, number, capital and symbol all show, with no hint which to fix first.
bad.wait: Press Create account to see this.

good.title: One line that shows the fix
good.text: “Finish the address, like maya@mail.com” shows the missing part by example.
good.wait: Press Create account to see this.

good.title: Only the length rule for now
good.text: Fix that first. The number rule shows up only if it’s still missing.
good.wait: Press Create account to see this.

bad.title: Wrong from the first digit
bad.text: Nobody types 10 digits at once, yet 1 key press already marks the field wrong.

bad.title: The same scolding nine times
bad.text: “Must be 10 digits” stays up for every digit until the tenth.
bad.wait: Type a digit in Phone to see this.

good.title: Quiet while people type
good.text: Nothing shows until they press Tab or click away, so a half-typed number is fine.

good.title: Shows on leaving, clears at ten
good.text: The tenth digit removes it at once, without leaving the field again.
good.wait: Type a few digits and press Tab to see this.

bad.title: “Invalid date” names no date
bad.text: Both fields are dates, so people may well change Check-in, the one that was fine.
bad.wait: Press Search stays to see this.

bad.title: Check-out falls before check-in
bad.text: 12 Nov to 10 Nov is a backwards stay, and nothing on screen says so.

good.title: Names the field and the rule
good.text: It quotes 12 Nov, so people know the date to beat.
good.wait: Press Search stays to see this.

good.title: One press sets 13 Nov
good.text: Set check-out to 13 Nov fixes the stay and runs the search.
good.wait: Press Search stays to see this.

bad.title: Gone after three seconds
bad.text: Anyone who looked away comes back to a list with only beach.jpg in it.
bad.wait: Press Upload photo.heic to see this.

bad.title: The list never mentions photo.heic
bad.text: Only beach.jpg shows, so the failed photo leaves no trace.

good.title: Not uploaded, right on the file
good.text: The row stays until people act, so one glance at the list tells them.
good.wait: Press Upload photo.heic to see this.

good.title: The size and the limit
good.text: 34 MB against a 20 MB limit, so people know how far off it is.
good.wait: Press Upload photo.heic to see this.

good.title: Compress and upload, right here
good.text: One press fixes it, with no other tool and no starting over.
good.wait: Press Upload photo.heic to see this.

bad.title: Restart rides on the toast
bad.text: Four seconds later the button is gone, and the update has no other way to finish.
bad.wait: Press Check for updates to see this.

bad.title: Checking again is the only way back
bad.text: People who missed it must ask again and catch the next toast.

good.title: Restart waits in the banner
good.text: No timer, so people can finish their note first.
good.wait: Press Check for updates to see this.

good.title: Later is a real choice
good.text: It answers “We’ll remind you tomorrow” instead of letting the chance slip by.
good.wait: Press Check for updates to see this.

bad.title: One press, three messages
bad.text: People asked for one upload and get a toast per file.

bad.title: The same news three times
bad.text: IMG_201, IMG_202 and IMG_203 each say “uploaded”, stacked over the page.
bad.wait: Press Upload 3 photos to see this.

good.title: One press, one message
good.text: The result reads as one job, the way people asked for it.

good.title: One toast that counts up
good.text: “Uploading 1 of 3…” turns into “3 photos uploaded” in the same spot.
good.wait: Press Upload 3 photos to see this.

bad.title: Files shows no sign of it
bad.text: Come back from Messages after the export and nothing says report.pdf is ready.

bad.title: A toast for an empty room
bad.text: It shows only if people stayed on Files, and leaves after three seconds.
bad.wait: Press Export report and wait 4 seconds to see this.

good.title: A 1 on Files while people are away
good.text: It waits for them to come back, and clears when they open Files.
good.wait: Press Export report, open Messages and wait 4 seconds to see this.

good.title: report.pdf marked Ready in the list
good.text: The result stays put, whether or not anyone saw the toast.
good.wait: Press Export report and wait 4 seconds to see this.

bad.title: A dialog for every delete
bad.text: By the second email people press Delete without reading what it says.
bad.wait: Press a trash button to see this.

bad.title: Two clicks per email
bad.text: Deleting two emails shows 4 here, and one slip still can’t be taken back.

good.title: Undo stays for five seconds
good.text: A slip is one press to fix, and the email returns to its old place.
good.wait: Press a trash button to see this.

good.title: One click per email
good.text: Deleting two emails shows 2 here, and Undo adds just one more.

bad.title: The top slot sells a Family plan
bad.text: People learn this stripe is for offers and stop reading it.

bad.title: Offline lands under the ad
bad.text: The one notice that matters now sits below the one people learned to skip.
bad.wait: Turn Online off to see this.

good.title: A dot on What’s new
good.text: The offer is one click away for people who want it, and quiet for the rest.

good.title: Offline gets the stripe to itself
good.text: It’s the only banner there, so people read it at once.
good.wait: Turn Online off to see this.

bad.title: No way to close the tip
bad.text: Once people know about /, it still takes a row above the plan.

bad.title: Day 2, same tip
bad.text: It comes back every day, so people learn to look past the top row.
bad.wait: Press Open the next day to see this.

good.title: A close button on the tip
good.text: Once read, one press gives the row back to the trip plan.

good.title: Day 2, no tip
good.text: The choice is remembered, so the tip doesn’t return on the next day.
good.wait: Close the tip, then press Open the next day to see this.

bad.title: Two banners before any numbers
bad.text: Read-only and a tip push the budget down while nothing is wrong yet.

bad.title: Offline makes it three
bad.text: The serious one joins the pile, and more of the budget drops out of view.
bad.wait: Turn Online off to see this.

good.title: One banner, the most serious
good.text: Read-only shows for now. Going offline takes its place.

good.title: 1 more holds the tip
good.text: The rest wait in a list, and the budget keeps its rows.

good.title: Offline takes the top
good.text: The button now says 2 more, and the sheet stays where it was.
good.wait: Turn Online off to see this.

bad.title: Send moves under the pointer
bad.text: Every 1.4 seconds the banner shifts the reply box, so clicks miss.

bad.title: Missed counts the slips
bad.text: Each click that lands beside Send adds one, and it climbs fast.

good.title: Send stays where people aim
good.text: Clicks during a reconnect still land on it.

good.title: Missed stays at 0
good.text: Every press on Send counts as sent.

bad.title: 3 on Shared, before and after
bad.text: It still says 3 after people have seen all of Lena’s photos.

bad.title: All three photos, already seen
bad.text: Beach day, Birthday cake and Sunset are on screen, yet the badge stays.

good.title: 3 until people open Shared
good.text: Then it’s gone, so the next badge means something new.

good.title: Seeing them is enough
good.text: Opening Shared counts as viewed, with no need to open each photo.
good.wait: Open Shared to see this.

bad.title: 48 on Files looks urgent
bad.text: It’s just a total, but it wears the same badge as real news.

bad.title: Shared’s 2 is lost among them
bad.text: The only new files look like every other count, so people open folders one by one.

good.title: 48 as plain text
good.text: The total is still there to read, but it doesn’t ask for a click.

good.title: Shared’s 2 is the only badge
good.text: People find Budget.xlsx and Trip.pdf on the first try.

bad.title: 486 stretches the badge wide
bad.text: Three digits already cover the icon’s corner, and Get new mail makes it 1286.

bad.title: The exact count, said twice
bad.text: Inbox · 486 unread already gives the number, so the badge adds only width.

good.title: 99+ fits on the icon
good.text: It stays the same width at 486 or 1,286, and still reads as “a lot”.

good.title: The exact count, where people read
good.text: Inbox · 486 unread sits at the top of the list the icon opens.

bad.title: A red 3 with no meaning
bad.text: Red reads as danger, so people worry about errors that are only updates.

bad.title: The gear says nothing on hover
bad.text: No label and no tooltip, so the only way to learn is to open it.

good.title: The same 3, not in red
good.text: The count reads as news, not as danger.

good.title: Settings, spelled out
good.text: The button names itself, and screen readers hear “Settings, 3 updates available”.

good.title: The tooltip says what it counts
good.text: People can decide whether to look now, before opening anything.
good.wait: Point at Settings to see this.
